repository.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser
repository.purpose: Browser authorization plugin registered as webex.authorization for the public browser build (re-exported by the @webex/plugin-authorization browser entry). It starts OAuth implicit-grant (public client, default) or authorization-code (confidential client) logins with a single-use CSRF token, parses an implicit-grant access token from the redirect URL hash during construction (CSRF check, URL scrubbing, next-tick hand-off to credentials), exchanges a host JWT for an access token through hydra jwt/login, mints HS256 guest JWTs, and redirects on logout. It does not exchange authorization codes.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser package entry
public_interfaces.audience: the @webex/plugin-authorization browser entry, the webex browser build, and browser applications
public_interfaces.notes: Importing the package imports @webex/internal-plugin-device and registers Authorization as public plugin 'authorization' with proxies isAuthorizing and isAuthenticating and the credentials config default clientType 'public'. The first registration of the name wins, so the first-party package takes 'authorization' when it is imported first.

public_interfaces.name: webex.authorization runtime methods
public_interfaces.audience: browser applications, webex-core credentials (JWT-mode refresh), and WebexCore#logout
public_interfaces.notes: initialize parses an implicit-grant token from the URL hash during construction and throws on redirect errors or CSRF failures. Only initiateLogin adds the CSRF token. No authorization code is exchanged in this package.

public_interfaces.name: credentials configuration default
public_interfaces.audience: integrators configuring Webex.init and webex-core credentials
public_interfaces.notes: clientType defaults to 'public' (implicit grant); 'confidential' switches initiateLogin to the authorization-code grant. Any other value is treated as public.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not rename or repurpose the sessionStorage key oauth2-csrf-token.
negative_guidance.why: A login started by one page load is checked on the next.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not move URL, storage, or CSRF work in initialize off the synchronous path.
negative_guidance.why: Redirect errors and CSRF failures must throw during construction, before a token reaches credentials.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not describe or rely on an authorization-code exchange in this package.
negative_guidance.why: initialize parses only the URL hash; no code exchange exists here.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat README.md or BROWSER-OAUTH-FLOW-GUIDE.md as the method, error, or refresh reference.
negative_guidance.why: Several claims differ from code or describe webex-core; see docs/adr/0001-keep-existing-docs-separate.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not run test:unit against a stale dist.
negative_guidance.why: The unit spec imports the package by name, which resolves main (dist/index.js).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: The developer confirmed no coverage gate applies; the legacy Jest config sets no threshold.

high.expectation: Source and unit test evidence both support the change, and the behavior has a case in test/unit/spec/authorization.js.

medium.expectation: Only source evidence exists, for example registration, requestAccessTokenFromJwt, createJwt, logout, or a hash without access_token. Pin current behavior with a characterization test before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source nor tests settle the question. Stop and report the gap.
